html:
The League of Corinth was a federation of Greek states set up by Philip II of Macedon in 338 and 337 BCE, after his victory at the Battle of Chaeronea. Its aim was to unite Greece under Macedonian leadership for a war against the Persian Empire.

The members swore to a common peace. They would not make war on one another or overthrow each other's governments, and a council of delegates met at Corinth to settle disputes. Philip was named hegemon, the leader, and commander of the war on Persia, which was meant to avenge the temples the Persians burned in 480 BCE. The Athenian writer Isocrates had urged just such a crusade for years. Sparta refused to join.

Philip was murdered in 336 BCE before the campaign began. The league chose Alexander as its new leader. When Thebes rebelled, the league approved its destruction (Alexander sacks Thebes). Greek troops then marched with Alexander in the conquest of Persia, though in practice the league was a tool of Macedonian control.
